top_choice_rationale: Cărtărescu (P001) is my first choice on a narrow judgment about cumulative formal achievement. On public knowledge, Blinding and Solenoid show a voice found nowhere else: a densely patterned prose that joins memory, the body and dream in one project across volumes, with a poetic imagination as its base. Unlike the case for Adonis, which is not on this slate, this case can be argued from the structure of the work. The citation should rest on the prose project and name poetry only as its foundation, because translation coverage of the poetry is thin. Open questions remain. They are whether the later volumes deepen or repeat the earlier architecture, and how much of the rhythmic Romanian sentence survives translation. I cannot settle either without close reading by readers of Romanian, and I have not read or verified any text for this stage. Carson (P002) is a close second. Her formal renewal across lyric, essay and verse novel is a serious alternative standard of sustained significance, and the citation should rest on the original core books. Tawada (P003) is third, because her formal method across Japanese and German is real but harder for me to assess across the whole corpus. No award (P000) is last, since several candidates with substantial and defensible cases remain.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile. My scholarly work on modern poetry, the fragment, exile literature and Celan is context only, not evidence of a preference. Ceremony speeches I have given were presented on behalf of the Academy and do not establish a personal vote. I disclose that my round 1 first choice, Adonis, is not on this slate and that my round 2 first choice moved to Cărtărescu.
